findings.problem: The workbench no-cookie assertion has no positive control. The Anthropic journey proves with a /cookie-probe that a non-omit session.fetch carries the planted cookie to its origin. The workbench block only checks that cookies.get returns the cookie. If the local session never sent that cookie to http://127.0.0.1:<port> for an unrelated reason, `cookie: undefined` would pass whatever credentials says. findings.problem: The code fails closed in several cases the spec does not describe; they should be listed in As built. (1) readAnthropic refuses with PROVIDER_INVALID_RESPONSE: a data payload that is not an object with a string `type`, even under `event: ping`; a content_block_start whose content_block lacks a string type; a delta on a known block whose `type` is missing or not a string; a non-null, non-string stop_reason. Section 5.4 only says unknown types are ignored. (2) A usage count that is not a non-negative safe integer is ignored, and an input sum past the safe integers leaves usage unset (tested, U3-R3/R7; not in spec 5.6). (3) screenCompletion turns a state whose data is not JSON into PROVIDER_PROTOCOL_ERROR (ARCHITECTURE says so; spec section 6 does not). (4) S-5 says 'only the owning adapter parses it'. Main's screen JSON.parses the data of any format to walk its leaves; spec section 6 designs this, so the requirement's wording should name the screen as the one other reader.
findings.fix: Record these in 'As built (Phase 2)'. No code change.

findings.problem: Small text points. (a) The hint and README say the 5.x models have 'up to 128K output tokens'. D7 found Anthropic's '64K' means 64,000, so 128K is likely 128,000, while the form accepts up to 200,000. A user who enters 131,072 gets a 400 that Test connection reports generically. (b) docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's Phase 2 paragraph keeps superseded interim clauses: 'src/main/anthropic.ts ... a skeleton until unit U3' and '`anthropic` answers NOT_IMPLEMENTED until U4', before later sentences that undo them. (c) README: 'Once a step returns thinking, the task's earlier steps must be sent back unchanged': D5f showed this account accepting a changed system prompt with signed thinking. The rule holds per E-12 for newer accounts and as Anthropic's advice, but 'must' is stronger than the live result. (d) profile.test picks its session from the stored profile.locality without the validateEndpoint comparison infer() makes. A pre-Phase-2 loopback anthropic row labelled local would be tested through the local session (spec section 7 known limit 2 covers only infer()). (e) npm run lint (eslint src tests scripts) does not cover e2e/; U5 ran eslint e2e by hand.

findings.problem: The S-1 state screen matches every stored vault value as a plain substring (vault.redact splits on each value; src/main/vault.ts:183-195), and that includes placeholder keys such as 'ollama', 'EMPTY' or 'lm-studio' that local OpenAI-compatible servers ask for. If any such value appears in an Anthropic tool step's thinking text, its text, or any key or string leaf of the state, the step fails with PROVIDER_PROTOCOL_ERROR. Thinking is free prose, so a run about a project that mentions the placeholder fails on every tool step. The spec's known limit (section 6, (1)) covers a real secret in a step but not this false positive on a short, common stored value. The README does not name it either.
findings.evidence: Scratch test tests/brk/cross.test.ts 'secret in thinking text of a tool step' ran the real engine, complete() and screenCompletion. The base was the D5-think-sonnet-step1 live recording with the thinking_delta changed to contain the stored value, and redact did a substring replace. Result: run failed with {"code":"PROVIDER_PROTOCOL_ERROR","message":"The provider returned a tool call or step Moonzila could not use safely ..."}. providerStateLeaves also returns object keys and type values ('type', 'text', 'thinking', 'tool_use', 'caller', 'direct'), so a stored value that is one of those words fails every step.
findings.reproduction: Save any profile whose key is a short common word (for example an OpenAI-compatible profile pointed at Ollama /v1 with key 'ollama'). Then run an Anthropic tool step whose thinking or text contains that word: screenCompletion(output, t => t.split('ollama').join('[redacted]')) throws PROVIDER_PROTOCOL_ERROR.
findings.fix: Either skip vault values below a minimum length (for example 16 characters) or values made only of [a-z-] in the state and content screen, or add this false positive to the spec's known limit (1) and to the README. Keep the tool-call rule as it is.

findings.problem: The history reserve's extra trimming loop (assembleContext with historyReserve) repeats the quadratic estimate that already existed: each dropped turn re-stringifies the whole request. It runs on every unfrozen step of an Anthropic tool run, synchronously in the engine process. The quadratic cost predates Phase 2; the reserve adds about 2.7x at small message sizes and makes it run in more cases.
findings.evidence: Scratch test tests/brk/reserve.test.ts: 500 turns (1000 messages), contextTokens 1,000,000, outputTokens 128,000. Size 2000: reserve off 442 ms, on 1183 ms. Size 20000: off 21353 ms, on 20263 ms. Size 200000: off 264445 ms, on 270576 ms. While this runs, the engine cannot answer main's 30 s control requests.
findings.reproduction: Call assembleContext({system, history: 500 turns of N-character user/assistant pairs, current: [user], tools: READ_TOOL_SPECS, contextTokens: 1e6, outputTokens: 128000, historyReserve: true}) and time it.
findings.fix: Optional: compute per-message estimates once and subtract when dropping a turn, which makes trimming linear. If not, record it for later; this is not a Phase 2 regression.

findings.problem: When the 600 s anthropic deadline fires in real Electron, the error is an AbortError ('The operation was aborted') if it hits mid-stream, or a TimeoutError if it hits before the headers. Both cross as PROVIDER_ERROR with the generic text 'Check the selected profile and project access'. The same text appears after retries on a 529 are used up, and for an Electron cut (net::ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING). A user whose step timed out after 10 minutes is told to check the profile. Electron itself imposes no shorter timeout.

Idling 620 s: '[600.4s] midstream THROW AbortError The operation was aborted after 600.033 s' and '[600.4s] ttfb THROW TimeoutError The operation was aborted due to timeout after 600.032 s'. A socket destroyed mid-stream: 'THROW Error net::ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING'; with a Content-Length: 'net::ERR_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH'.
findings.reproduction: Run the harness above with IDLE_S=620: dbus-run-session -- xvfb-run -a electron --no-sandbox --disable-gpu .
findings.fix: No code change is required for correctness. Record that the deadline and retry exhaustion show the generic PROVIDER_ERROR text. A dedicated message needs a public mapping (F-21), so keep it with the recorded-for-later items.

findings.problem: A stream that ends cleanly (no transport error) before any text block, for example a cut during the thinking block, is read as outcome 'incomplete' with content ''. The engine stores an empty partial assistant message, and the renderer shows nothing for it (MessageItem returns null). In real Electron an abrupt cut raises a net:: error instead, so no message is stored. Only a server or proxy that closes the chunked body properly without message_stop reaches the empty-row path.
findings.evidence: tests/brk/cross.test.ts '529 (retry-after 0) then a stream cut mid-thinking': a 529 with retry-after 0 was retried once, then the step-2 body ended cleanly mid-thinking. The run failed with PROVIDER_ERROR and the stored messages ended with 'assistant(partial):' (empty). A reset mid data line stored no partial. The frozen run's earlier signature was not found in state.sqlite, -wal or -shm (byte scan empty).
findings.reproduction: Serve D5-think-sonnet-step2.response.raw truncated before its first content_block_stop, with a clean close, to step 2 of a frozen run.
findings.fix: Optional: skip storing an empty incomplete assistant message. This is pre-existing behaviour for every kind.

findings.problem: The F-17 estimate counts a whole-replay message as JSON.stringify of a string that already holds JSON. Every quote, backslash and newline inside the state's data is escaped a second time, so thinking text with many quotes or newlines is overestimated. That can end a frozen run with CONTEXT_LIMIT earlier than the request needs. Signatures (base64) and the empty thinking in the live recordings are not affected.
findings.evidence: src/engine/context.ts estimated() returns {role, providerState: state.data}, then estimateInput JSON.stringifies it. The state data is the JSON text built by toolCallsOutcome.
findings.reproduction: Compare estimateInput on a message whose state thinking text is 100 KB of '"\n' with the byte length of the encoder's assistant entry.
findings.fix: Count JSON.parse(state.data).content, the value the encoder sends, instead of the data string. Otherwise note that the error is conservative.

findings.problem: The tool-call secret check that moved unchanged into screenCompletion (src/main/provider-screen.ts:33-36, rule 1) still compares the JSON text of the calls. Suppose a vault secret contains a double quote, a backslash or a control character, and it appears in a tool input from a chat kind (openai-compatible or ollama, which carry no provider state). JSON.stringify escapes those characters, so the secret never matches the text, the screen passes, and the call runs (for example run_command). It is then stored in messages.tool_calls and in the tool.started event, and session.read returns it to the renderer in clear. For the anthropic kind the state's leaf scan does catch it, because every tool_use input is also in the state. The gap was already there before Phase 2 and the spec records it (more-models-phase2.md:1117, 'Pre-existing: the tool-call secret check reads JSON text'). However, AGENTS.md's 'Tokens never reach the engine, DB, events, logs, renderer ... in clear' row is written without that exception, and on HEAD 5e82997 the row now cites provider-screen tests for the 'escaped' case.
findings.evidence: Ran a scratch vitest file in the worktree at 2d3fa59: for each secret in ['key"with-quote-1234', 'key\\with-backslash-1234', 'key\twith-tab-1234'], redact = text => text.split(secret).join('[redacted]'), then await screenCompletion({content:'', outcome:'tool_calls', toolCalls:[{id:'c1', name:'run_command', input:{command:`curl -H "Authorization: ${secret}"`}}]}, redact). Output for all three: 'PASSED SCREEN; input still holds secret: true' (1 test passed, no throw).
findings.reproduction: In tests/, call screenCompletion with a completion that has no providerState and whose toolCalls[0].input holds a secret containing " or \, using a redact that replaces that secret. The call resolves and nothing throws. Run the same shape through Application with a chat-kind profile: the call is stored, and session.read returns the secret's decoded value.
findings.fix: In rule 1, screen the leaves of the calls rather than their JSON text, for example `providerStateLeaves(JSON.stringify(output.toolCalls))`; keys are included, and numbers are already covered by the JSON-text check, which can stay too. Add a provider-screen case with a secret containing " and one containing \ in a chat-kind tool input, and show it red against the current JSON-text check. Until that lands, qualify the AGENTS.md tokens row with this exception or point it at the recorded item.

findings.problem: An anthropic profile saved through IPC before Phase 2 with a loopback endpoint has locality 'local' stored. Phase 2 makes every anthropic endpoint external, but stored rows keep their old label. For such a profile the engine's local-only checks at run.start (application.ts:237) and before each step (assertRunPolicy) read the stored label, so they admit the run in a local-only conversation. The user's prompt is stored and the run starts. Only main's comparison in infer(), `inferred.locality !== context.profile.locality` → INVALID_ENDPOINT (index.ts:94), stops the fetch, and the user then sees the generic PROVIDER_ERROR text. No byte leaves the machine, but two of the three layers named in the invariant do not hold for this row: run.start and before each step. Main's guard is pinned only by a source-line-order test (anthropic-transport.test.ts:308-331), not by behaviour. profile.test for such a row also picks localSession because of the label, and the profile list shows the profile as 'Local'. The spec records this as known limit (2) in section 7.
findings.evidence: Read src/engine/application.ts:234-237 (run.start uses publicProfile(...).locality) and :494-496 (assertRunPolicy uses the stored locality). Read src/main/index.ts:91-95: assertConversationPolicy runs with the stored locality, then the label is compared with validateEndpoint. git show 3735096:src/main/inference.ts: validateEndpoint returned 'local' for any loopback kind, and src/shared/params.ts:24 already accepted kind 'anthropic' in profile.save. findings.reproduction: Use Store.putProfile({kind:'anthropic', endpoint:'http://127.0.0.1:9/v1', locality:'local', ...}) in a project whose policy is local-only, then call run.start. findings.problem: The vault grant for inference still lasts 125 s (index.ts:102), sized for the 120 s chat deadline. An anthropic call can last up to 600 s and can retry twice. withSecret checks the grant only on entry, so a retry can send the key after the grant has expired. This stays within withSecret's callback and only in the Authorization header, and a credential replacement or a policy change aborts the call through capability.stop. So the invariant 'keys only in Authorization within withSecret' holds, but the grant's expiry no longer bounds how long the key is in use. REQUIREMENTS-P2 F-22 records this.
findings.evidence: src/main/vault.ts:156-161 (authorized() is checked on entry only); src/main/anthropic.ts:382 (timeoutMs 600_000); src/main/inference.ts post() retries inside the same invoke closure; REQUIREMENTS-P2.md F-22 says 'the grant is checked on entry only, so the 125 s grant ... does not bound a call'.
findings.reproduction: Reading the code is enough: the first anthropic attempt gets a 503 at t≈124 s; post() waits 1 s and fetches again with the same Authorization header after the grant's expiresAt.
findings.fix: No change is required for the invariant. Optionally, size the inference grant from the kind's timeoutMs, or check vault.authorized before each retry, so that expiry again bounds use of the key.

findings.problem: Nothing tests that complete() hands post() the kind's own deadline. If complete() passes `deadline: started + 120_000` instead of `started + part.timeoutMs`, an Anthropic retry whose retry-after wait ends between 120 s and 600 s is refused at once with PROVIDER_HTTP_503 or PROVIDER_HTTP_429, when it should wait and retry. This breaks F-14 (5xx and 429 waits honour an integer retry-after) together with F-22 (one 600 s deadline for every attempt of an anthropic call). The 600 s timer itself is tested (I11 was killed). The deadline value post() uses to decide whether a wait fits is not.
findings.evidence: Mutation I12 in src/main/inference.ts line 289: `deadline: started + part.timeoutMs,` changed to `deadline: started + 120_000,`. The mutant SURVIVED both the scoped files (provider-transport, anthropic-transport, anthropic, ollama-locality, provider-stream) and the full set of 10 named files (FULL=1 rerun: status 0). I wrote a probe test that is not committed: `timed([() => refusedWith(503, {'retry-after':'300'}), okStream])` with fake timers advanced by 400 s. It passes on 2d3fa59 with at=[0,300000] and settledAt=300000. On the mutant it fails: `expected [ +0 ] to deeply equal [ +0, 300000 ]`, meaning one fetch, then PROVIDER_HTTP_503.
findings.reproduction: Create a worktree at 2d3fa59. Add the probe above to tests/anthropic-transport.test.ts, inside or beside describe('retries through complete()'), reusing its timed() and refusedWith() helpers. Run `npx vitest run tests/anthropic-transport.test.ts`: it passes. Then apply `sed -i 's/deadline: started + part.timeoutMs,/deadline: started + 120_000,/' src/main/inference.ts` and run again: the probe fails while the 503 tests at 1 s/2 s and the 600 s stall tests still pass.
findings.fix: Add the probe as a regression test in tests/anthropic-transport.test.ts: a 503 (or 429) with retry-after 300 makes a second fetch at 300 000 ms and completes. Optionally add a companion: retry-after 700 is refused at once as PROVIDER_HTTP_503, which pins the 600 s bound from the other side. Name the mutation in the guard comment, as the neighbouring tests do.

findings.problem: A surviving mutation that is equivalent in practice: complete() hands post() `stop: options.signal`, and changing it to the joined Stop-plus-deadline signal survives. pause() reads `stop` only to tell a Stop from the deadline when the joined signal aborts during a wait. post() never starts a wait that would end at or after `started + timeoutMs`, so the deadline cannot fire during a wait except through a sub-millisecond gap between arming the timer and reading `started`. Even then, RUN_CANCELLED and a TimeoutError both reach the engine as PROVIDER_ERROR (inferenceErrorCode). So the wiring is unobservable. The post()-level test covers pause()'s distinction directly (I8 and I17 were killed).
findings.evidence: Mutation I19 in src/main/inference.ts line 289: `stop: options.signal, deadline:` changed to `stop: AbortSignal.any([options.signal, deadline.signal]), deadline:`. It SURVIVED both the scoped run and the FULL=1 run over the 10 files.
findings.reproduction: Apply the edit and run `npx vitest run` on tests/provider-transport.test.ts, tests/anthropic-transport.test.ts and the other 8 named files: all pass.
findings.fix: No code change needed. Optionally add a note in the complete() comment that `stop` must be the caller's signal alone, or a source-pin test, if the team wants the wiring guarded against a future refactor that removes the before-deadline check.

findings.problem: Two guards in toolCallsOutcome (src/main/anthropic.ts) duplicate later checks, so removing either is an equivalent mutation. The only difference: a state over PROVIDER_STATE_MAX with an unsigned thinking block gives PROVIDER_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE instead. (b) The 'no tool_use block' check at line 297 is repeated by InferenceToolCallsSchema.min(1) at line 309-310, which gives the same invalid().
findings.evidence: N26 (line 301 removed) and N61 (`if (!blocks.some(block => block.fields.type === 'tool_use')) return invalid();` removed) both SURVIVED the scoped run and the FULL=1 run over the 10 files.
findings.reproduction: Remove either line and run `npx vitest run tests/anthropic.test.ts tests/anthropic-transport.test.ts`: all pass.
